evals.name: projection-total-spec
evals.prompt: A projection builds `OrderSummary` (Total) from `OrderCreated` and `ItemAdded(decimal Price)` events on one order stream. Write a Cratis Specification class with ReadModelScenario that proves two items priced 9.99 and 4.50 give a total of 14.49. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A new ReadModelScenario<OrderSummary> in Establish, seeded with Given.ForEventSource(...).Events(...), no separate When, asserting Instance.Total with ShouldEqual and disposing the scenario.
assertions: Creates a new ReadModelScenario<OrderSummary> per specification.
Seeds events with scenario.Given.ForEventSource(id).Events(...) and does not use a separate When, since Given is the act.
Asserts on scenario.Instance with ShouldEqual (not ShouldBe) because the scenario has no Should assertions of its own.

evals.name: null-or-multiple-instances
evals.prompt: (a) `scenario.Instance` is null after seeding events; (b) a different spec seeding events on two event sources gets MultipleInstancesMaterialized when reading Instance. Explain each and the fix. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: (a) No seeded event matched the projection, so check key resolution before property mapping; (b) Instance is ambiguous when more than one instance exists, use InstanceForEventSourceId(id) or Instances, or seed one source.
assertions: States that a null Instance means no seeded event matched the projection so nothing was created, and to check key resolution before property mapping.
States that MultipleInstancesMaterialized means the seeded events produced more than one instance.
Recommends InstanceForEventSourceId(id) or the Instances dictionary, or seeding a single source.

evals.name: pinned-instance-trap
evals.prompt: A spec uses `Given.ForEventSource(id).ReadModel(instance)` to pin a materialized instance and then asserts properties; it passes but the production projection is broken. Why, and what coverage should a good projection spec have? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Pinning an instance means the projection never ran; seed events instead. Cover every property, every subscribed event, removal events asserting absence, and partial updates leaving other properties unchanged.
assertions: States that pinning a read-model instance bypasses the projection so the projection under question never ran; the spec should seed events.
Says every property should be asserted in at least one specification and every subscribed event should have a specification.
Says every removal or clearing event needs a specification asserting absence (Instance is null or the child is gone).
Says a later event updating only some properties needs a specification showing the others are unchanged.

evals.name: reducer-spec-scope
evals.prompt: For a pure reducer decision `AccountBalance.Reduce(FundsDebited, current)`, should the spec use ReadModelScenario? What does ReadModelScenario not prove regardless? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Use Specification plus a direct call with explicit event and current state by default; add ReadModelScenario only when dispatch, filtering, metadata or wiring contribute proof. Scenarios substitute storage, observer lifecycle and compliance and do not prove real-kernel registration, replay, transport, encryption, erasure or migration.
assertions: Says pure reducer decisions should use Specification and a direct call passing the event and current state explicitly.
Says ReadModelScenario is added only where event dispatch, filtering, metadata or read-model wiring contribute proof.
States that scenarios do not prove real-kernel registration, replay, transport, encryption, erasure or migration.
